q: Is hot-rolled coil and plate under CN 7208 covered by CBAM?
title: CBAM CN 7208: hot-rolled coil and plate
short: Yes. Flat-rolled iron or non-alloy steel, hot-rolled, 600 mm or wider, is CN 7208 and covered under the Chapter 72 line of Annex I. Direct emissions only. A rolling mill that buys slabs passes on the slab maker's figure as a precursor and adds its own reheating fuel.
audience: Indian HR coil and plate exporters, and mills rolling bought slabs

p: Yes. CN 7208 hot-rolled flat products 600 mm wide or more are covered. Narrower hot-rolled strip moves to 7211, also covered. Only direct emissions count for iron and steel.

ul: Crude steel (slab) you made or bought. A bought slab needs its maker's embedded emissions per tonne.
Pig iron, DRI and the three covered ferro-alloys, if you make the steel yourself.

sections.h: The India default value for CN 7208
p: 4.280 t CO2e per tonne, direct emissions only. The India table marks it (C), the blast furnace and basic oxygen furnace route, which decides the benchmark deducted against it. The importer adds a mark-up of 10% for goods imported in 2026, 20% in 2027 and 30% from 2028, so a 2026 tonne goes in at 4.708. That is the figure your buyer pays on if you send nothing usable.

sections.h: What to send your EU importer
ul: Direct embedded emissions per tonne of coil or plate, in tonnes of CO2, for the period the importer asks about.
The production route and the installation's name, location and, if registered, its CBAM registry ID.
Each precursor's embedded emissions and quantity per tonne, and who made it if you bought it.
Whether a verifier accredited for CBAM has checked the figure. The importer can only use actual values that are verified.

p: Leaving out the reheating furnace. Rolling mills burn natural gas, LPG or furnace oil to reheat slabs, and those are direct emissions of the rolling step. Add them to the slab figure, per tonne of coil shipped, allowing for yield loss.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and purchase invoices into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for. It does not file CBAM declarations or verify emissions.

example.title: 1,000 t of HR coil imported in Q3 2026 on the default
lines: Default with the 2026 mark-up: 4.280 x 1.10 = 4.708 t CO2e per tonne
Free allocation adjustment: 0.975 (CBAM factor) x 1.0 (correction factor) x 1.370 (benchmark, CN 7208, BF/BOF route) = 1.336
Certificates owed: 4.708 minus 1.336 = 3.372 per tonne, 3,372 for the shipment
Cost at the Q3 2026 price of EUR 82.32: about EUR 278 per tonne, about EUR 277,600 for the shipment
example.note: The correction factor of 1.0 is the Commission's listed value in Guidance No. 4; if the final 2026 value is lower, the deduction shrinks and the cost rises.

reviewNote: Default values, benchmarks and the certificate price are set by the Commission; re-check the default values annex after any correcting act and the price each quarter.
